body.statement:
For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\), use a normalized quasi-uniform spline basis of degree sufficient for \(C^s\) approximation and a growing dimension satisfying
\[
J_n\to\infty,\qquad
\sqrt n\,J_n^{-2s}\to0,\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}{\sqrt n}\to0,\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n}{n}\to0,
\]
with \(\alpha_a=0\) under the bounded-support convention.  Then the data-driven clip is asymptotically inactive when the propensity is bounded away from zero and is first-order negligible otherwise under \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\).  The cross-fitted likelihood construction satisfies
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n{\rm IF}_a(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1)
\]
jointly over \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), with covariance \(E_P[{\rm IF}_a{\rm IF}_{a'}^\top]\).
body.justification: The Gaussian branch retains shared first-stage covariance and is now centered at the correct untrimmed quantile.
body.gap: Firpo establishes the regular-overlap result; the present branch allows finite inverse moments without strict overlap and is supporting machinery for mixed regimes.
body.consumer: It supplies the regular component of a QTE whose other arm can have an infinitely divisible limit.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the constrained cross-fitted likelihood projection expansion and empirical-clipping negligibility for every finite-variance arm under the corrected learner.
obligation.obstruction: Finite \(E_P[1/\pi_a(X)]\) makes the limiting Riesz score square integrable but does not itself justify inversion of the growing random Hessian or replacement of the finite-sieve Riesz projection by its limit. Those are the load-bearing steps that create the learned-propensity influence term.
obligation.attempted: Derived the exact Bernoulli log-link information geometry, its Riesz representer for the signed propensity functional, the resulting score, and its algebraic recombination with the oracle quantile score. Checked that the displayed bias and nonlinear-remainder orders are compatible with the frozen tuning conditions.
obligation.partial_result:
The required Gaussian first-stage term has an exact likelihood geometry.  For a perturbation \(g\) of the log propensity, the Bernoulli log-link score and information inner product are
\[
s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},
\qquad
\mathcal I_a(g_1,g_2)
=E_P\!\left[\frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
\]
The derivative of the signed functional is
\(\dot L_a(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\).  Its Riesz representer in this information geometry is
\[
r_{a,\tau}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)},
\]
because \(\mathcal I_a(r_{a,\tau},g)=\dot L_a(g)\).  Therefore
\[
s_{r_{a,\tau}}(O)
=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}m_{a,\tau}(X)}{\pi_a(X)}.
\]
The finite-inverse-moment assumption and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\) imply
\[
E_P\{s_{r_{a,\tau}}^2\}
=E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2
\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]<\infty.
\]
Thus, if \(r_{a,\tau,J_n}\) is the information projection onto the corrected likelihood sieve, density of the spline spaces gives
\(s_{r_{a,\tau,J_n}}\to s_{r_{a,\tau}}\) in \(L^2(P)\).  The likelihood projection would then yield
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)},dP_X(x)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\]
Subtracting this expression from the oracle weighted quantile score gives exactly
\[
\mathrm{IF}_a(O;\tau)=\frac1{f_a(\tau)}
\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)+
\frac{\mathbf1\{A=a\}\{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y)-m_{a,\tau}(X)\}}
{\pi_a(X)}\right].
\]
The displayed tuning restrictions have the correct arithmetic for this route:
the product approximation bias is \(O(J_n^{-2s})\), the reciprocal-likelihood quadratic remainder is \(O_P(J_n^{\alpha_a}/n)\), and the weakest local information requires \(J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n/n\to0\).  After multiplication by \(\sqrt n\), the first two terms vanish under the frozen conditions.  What remains unproved is precisely the constrained random-Hessian expansion that justifies the projection display for the corrected sample map, together with first-order negligibility of its empirical clip.  Neither conclusion is a consequence of finite inverse moments alone.
